nodes.summary: Stand up the Go module, package layout, and the CLI entry contract everything else builds into.
nodes.instructions:
Create the root go.mod (Go 1.22 or newer, no third-party requirements) and the package layout:
cmd/csvstat (package main), internal/cli (Run(args []string, stdout, stderr io.Writer) int),
internal/csvdata (reading, trimming, nulls, validation), internal/infer (type inference),
internal/profile (statistics), internal/freq (frequency listing), internal/decimal (exact
rounding). Only main calls os.Exit. Document the exit-code table (0, 1, 2, 3) and the rule that
a failing command writes nothing to stdout and one diagnostic line to stderr. Create bin/ for
launchers. Do not read sources/run.sh or any data file from application code.
nodes.name: Stand up the Go module, package layout, and the CLI entry contract everything else builds into.

nodes.summary: Build the csvstat executable from the application root with the standard library only.
nodes.instructions:
Add cmd/csvstat/main.go that calls cli.Run(os.Args[1:], os.Stdout, os.Stderr) and passes the
result to os.Exit. Provide a minimal Run so that go build -o <path> ./cmd/csvstat succeeds from
the module root. Verify that go.mod has no require lines.
nodes.name: Build the csvstat executable from the application root with the standard library only.

nodes.summary: Parse options that precede exactly one file argument.
nodes.instructions:
In internal/cli use a local flag.FlagSet with flag.ContinueOnError and its output sent to the
stderr writer. Define --column, --freq, and --top. Exactly one positional file is required: no
file or more than one file exits 2 with nothing on stdout and one stderr diagnostic line.
nodes.name: Parse options that precede exactly one file argument.

nodes.summary: Read a UTF-8 RFC 4180 CSV file with encoding/csv and trim header names and values.
nodes.instructions:
Implement csvdata.Read returning the trimmed header and the trimmed records. Use encoding/csv
with FieldsPerRecord set to -1 so the record width can be checked by the next story with line
numbers. Trim leading and trailing spaces from every header name and value before any other
rule. Quoted fields containing commas and quotes decode as RFC 4180 specifies.
nodes.name: Read a UTF-8 RFC 4180 CSV file with encoding/csv and trim header names and values.

nodes.summary: Classify null values: empty, NA, N/A, NULL ignoring case.
nodes.instructions:
Implement csvdata.IsNull on trimmed values: true for the empty string and for NA, N/A, NULL in
any letter case; false for everything else, including 0, nan, and none. The helper is the single
null rule used by every statistic.
nodes.name: Classify null values: empty, NA, N/A, NULL ignoring case.

nodes.summary: Reject unknown options, missing option values, and invalid option combinations with exit 2.
nodes.instructions:
Exit 2, nothing on stdout, one stderr line, for: unknown option, an option missing its value,
--top that is not a positive integer (zero, negative, non-numeric), --top without --freq, and
--column together with --freq. Validation completes before the file is opened, so a usage error
wins over a missing file. --top defaults to 5 when --freq is given.
nodes.name: Reject unknown options, missing option values, and invalid option combinations with exit 2.

nodes.summary: Reject an empty file, an empty or repeated header name, or a ragged record with exit 3.
nodes.instructions:
Reject with exit 3, nothing on stdout, and exactly one stderr line naming the file (and the line
number of the offending record when a record is ragged): an empty file (no records), an empty
header name after trimming, a repeated header name, any record whose field count differs from the
header, and a CSV syntax error reported by encoding/csv. A header with no data records is valid.
nodes.name: Reject an empty file, an empty or repeated header name, or a ragged record with exit 3.

nodes.summary: Exit 1 with no stdout when the file cannot be opened or read.
nodes.instructions:
When the file cannot be opened or read (missing path, a directory, no permission) exit 1 with
nothing on stdout and one stderr line naming the file. This is distinct from exit 3, which is
reserved for content that was read but rejected. Usage errors (exit 2) are owned by CLI-001 and
CLI-002.
nodes.name: Exit 1 with no stdout when the file cannot be opened or read.

nodes.summary: Provide the POSIX bin/test.sh that runs go vet and go test.
nodes.instructions:
Write bin/test.sh in POSIX sh. It changes to the application root, runs go vet ./... and then
go test ./..., and exits non-zero if either fails. Add at least one Go test so the suite is
non-empty. Later stories add their own tests beside their code.
nodes.name: Provide the POSIX bin/test.sh that runs go vet and go test.

nodes.summary: Build the csvstat executable from the application root with the standard library only.
nodes.instructions:
Add cmd/csvstat/main.go that calls cli.Run(os.Args[1:], os.Stdout, os.Stderr) and passes the
result to os.Exit. Provide a minimal Run so that go build -o <path> ./cmd/csvstat succeeds from
the module root. Verify that go.mod has no require lines.
nodes.name: Build the csvstat executable from the application root with the standard library only.

nodes.summary: Parse options that precede exactly one file argument.
nodes.instructions:
In internal/cli use a local flag.FlagSet with flag.ContinueOnError and its output sent to the
stderr writer. Define --column, --freq, and --top. Exactly one positional file is required: no
file or more than one file exits 2 with nothing on stdout and one stderr diagnostic line.
nodes.name: Parse options that precede exactly one file argument.

nodes.summary: Read a UTF-8 RFC 4180 CSV file with encoding/csv and trim header names and values.
nodes.instructions:
Implement csvdata.Read returning the trimmed header and the trimmed records. Use encoding/csv
with FieldsPerRecord set to -1 so the record width can be checked by the next story with line
numbers. Trim leading and trailing spaces from every header name and value before any other
rule. Quoted fields containing commas and quotes decode as RFC 4180 specifies.
nodes.name: Read a UTF-8 RFC 4180 CSV file with encoding/csv and trim header names and values.

nodes.summary: Classify null values: empty, NA, N/A, NULL ignoring case.
nodes.instructions:
Implement csvdata.IsNull on trimmed values: true for the empty string and for NA, N/A, NULL in
any letter case; false for everything else, including 0, nan, and none. The helper is the single
null rule used by every statistic.
nodes.name: Classify null values: empty, NA, N/A, NULL ignoring case.

nodes.summary: Reject unknown options, missing option values, and invalid option combinations with exit 2.
nodes.instructions:
Exit 2, nothing on stdout, one stderr line, for: unknown option, an option missing its value,
--top that is not a positive integer (zero, negative, non-numeric), --top without --freq, and
--column together with --freq. Validation completes before the file is opened, so a usage error
wins over a missing file. --top defaults to 5 when --freq is given.
nodes.name: Reject unknown options, missing option values, and invalid option combinations with exit 2.

nodes.summary: Reject an empty file, an empty or repeated header name, or a ragged record with exit 3.
nodes.instructions:
Reject with exit 3, nothing on stdout, and exactly one stderr line naming the file (and the line
number of the offending record when a record is ragged): an empty file (no records), an empty
header name after trimming, a repeated header name, any record whose field count differs from the
header, and a CSV syntax error reported by encoding/csv. A header with no data records is valid.
nodes.name: Reject an empty file, an empty or repeated header name, or a ragged record with exit 3.

nodes.summary: Exit 1 with no stdout when the file cannot be opened or read.
nodes.instructions:
When the file cannot be opened or read (missing path, a directory, no permission) exit 1 with
nothing on stdout and one stderr line naming the file. This is distinct from exit 3, which is
reserved for content that was read but rejected. Usage errors (exit 2) are owned by CLI-001 and
CLI-002.
nodes.name: Exit 1 with no stdout when the file cannot be opened or read.

nodes.summary: Provide the POSIX bin/test.sh that runs go vet and go test.
nodes.instructions:
Write bin/test.sh in POSIX sh. It changes to the application root, runs go vet ./... and then
go test ./..., and exits non-zero if either fails. Add at least one Go test so the suite is
non-empty. Later stories add their own tests beside their code.
nodes.name: Provide the POSIX bin/test.sh that runs go vet and go test.
